summary: 13th Dalai Lama worked in Buddhist studies, Tibetology, and religious studies. He studied under Agvan Dorzhiev, Pa Ri Rabsal, Tertön Sogyal, Lobsang Lungtok Tenzin Thinley, Gendun Tendzin Gyatso, Jampa Gyatso, Ngawang Pelden Chokyi Gyeltsen, and Yeshe Chopel.
Working in Buddhist studies and Tibetology, 16th Karmapa Rangjung Rigpe Dorje studied under Kalu Rinpoche, the 1st Beru Khyentse, and Tulku Urgyen Rinpoche.
19th Kushok Bakula Rinpoche was a scholar in Buddhist studies and Tibetology. He studied under Ngawang Lobzang Gyatso, Khangsar Dorje Chang, and Jamphel Yeshe Gyaltsen.

Specializing in Tibetology and Buddhist studies, 2nd Beru Khyentse studied under Dzongsar Khenpo Chimey Rinpoche, Kalu Rinpoche, the 16th Karmapa Rangjung Rigpe Dorje, Khunu Lama Tenzin Gyaltsen, Sakya Trizin Ngawang Kunga, and Dilgo Khyentse.
A Drö Khenpo Yeshe Gyatso studied under Jamgon Ju Mipham Gyatso and Khenpo Shenga.

A. A. Krishnaswami Ayyangar worked in Indology. He studied at Pachaiyappa's College (~1907–1911), where he held a post from 1911 to 1918, before serving as a professor at the University of Mysore (1918–1947).

A. Aiyappan worked in Indology and history and archaeology. He studied at the University of Madras (~1925–1927), served as Superintendent at the Government Museum, Chennai (~1940–1960), and held a post at the University of Kerala (~1969–1972).
A. B. Gajendragadkar worked in Indology. He served as a Lecturer on Sanskrit at Karnatak Arts College and as a Senior Dakshina Fellow at Deccan College Post-Graduate and Research Institute.

A scholar of Buddhist studies, Sinology, and Japanology, Muller completed his Ph.D. at Stony Brook University. He held positions at Toyo Gakuen University (1994–2008), the University of Tokyo (2005; 2008–2019), and Musashino University (2019).
A. G. Mohan is an Indology and religious studies scholar who studied under Tirumalai Krishnamacharya (~1971–1989). He founded the Krishnamacharya Yoga Mandiram in 1976.

A. K. Narain was a scholar of Indology, history and archaeology, and Buddhist studies. He earned degrees from Banaras Hindu University and SOAS University of London, later serving as a professor at the University of Wisconsin-Madison (1971–1987).

A. K. Ramanujan worked in linguistics and Indology. He earned degrees from Maharaja's College, Mysore and Indiana University, and was a long-serving professor at the University of Chicago (1962–1993).

A. N. Narasimhia specialized in linguistics and Indology, earning a PhD from SOAS University of London under Ralph Lilley Turner (~1930–1933). He held posts at the University of Mysore and Maharaja's College, Mysore.

A. V. Williams Jackson specialized in Indology and Iranian and Central Asian studies. He studied at Columbia University and Martin Luther University of Halle-Wittenberg, later serving as a fellow (1883–1886) and professor (1895–1935) at Columbia University.

Aaron P. Proffitt works in Buddhist studies and Japanology. He earned his master's at the University of Colorado and his Ph.D. at the University of Michigan, becoming an assistant professor at the University at Albany, SUNY (~2015).

Abanindranath Tagore worked in history, archaeology, and Indology. He studied at Sanskrit Collegiate School, Sanskrit College and University, and Government College of Art & Craft, and held a post at the University of Calcutta (~1921–1929).

Abdur Rehman is an Indology, history, and archaeology scholar who completed a PhD at the Australian National University under Arthur Llewellyn Basham. By 1988, he held an assistant professorship at the University of Peshawar.

Abel Bergaigne worked in Indology and linguistics, studying under Michel Bréal and Eugène-Louis Hauvette-Besnault. He held posts at École Pratique des Hautes Études (~1869–1877), Sorbonne University (1877), and the University of Paris (~1885–1888).

Abhiraj Rajendra Mishra is an Indology scholar who studied under Rambhadracharya. He headed the Sanskrit department at Himachal Pradesh University, served as Vice-Chancellor at Sampurnanand Sanskrit University, and was a visiting professor at the University of Indonesia.

Abigail I. MacBain is a scholar of religious studies, Japanology, and Buddhist studies. She earned an MA from McMaster University, where her teachers included Mark Rowe, James A. Benn, Shayne Clarke, Mark MacWilliams, and Michael Greenwald.
